*Trump said Nvidia's ($NVDA) stock decline influenced his decision to intervene, expressing confidence in the market's response to Jensen Huang's reinstatement and calling it “a great thing for our country and even for the world.”*

• *Second Term* — Trump said Huang was extremely happy to return and calls it “his second term.”
• *Chip Roadmap* — Trump said Blackwell would be obsolete in a year and that Nvidia has two upcoming chips that are “blowing Blackwell away,” emphasizing Huang's importance to the company.
• *Return* — Trump has not spoken with Huang since his reinstatement but expects to speak with him before Monday, when he believes Huang essentially resumes his duties.
• *National Security* — Questioned about Huang's potential security risk and the lack of a proper DOJ investigation, Trump cited information available to him without disclosing specifics.

*Hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform, one of the military's largest cloud systems, potentially exposing sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data, Reuters reports, citing three people familiar with the matter.*

• *Cloud Providers* — Cloud One combines computing resources from Microsoft *($MSFT)*, Amazon *($AMZN)*, Oracle *($ORCL)* and Alphabet *($GOOGL)*. Leidos *($LDOS)* replaced SAIC *($SAIC)* as prime contractor in 2025.
• *Sensitive Systems* — The platform supports military command and control, air defense, weapons tracking, personnel records and logistics.
• *Operational Disruption* — The breach was discovered during system upgrades within the past month. Application migrations and software updates have been halted, while some users lost administrator privileges.
• *Investigation* — U.S. Cyber Command has reportedly been called in to assess the damage. The hackers' identities, the full extent of the breach and whether any data was stolen remain unknown. The Air Force declined to comment on the platform's security status.

*Nvidia ($NVDA) Blackwell chips have been installed at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, Bloomberg reports, citing Chinese regulatory filings. The discovery marks the first documented presence of Blackwell chips at the facility, despite U.S. export restrictions.*

• *Blackwell Discovery* — Shanghai Shuoyao pledged a GB300 NVL72 rack manufactured by Gigabyte as collateral for a $14M bank loan. Shanghai Kezhan disclosed a GB200 server when securing a 90M yuan loan from a government-owned financing firm.
• *Additional Hardware* — Kezhan also disclosed 32 servers containing restricted H200 chips. A separate $11M shipment from Malaysia was labeled as storage equipment, although its customs code and pricing suggest it may have contained computing servers.
• *Alice Huang Connection* — Shuoyao confirmed it provides services to Megaspeed, while Kezhan's majority owner, Japan-based NeXPower, is reportedly controlled by Alice Huang. The facility is designed to accommodate up to 800,000 servers.
• *Unresolved Questions* — How the Blackwell hardware reached China remains unclear. Bloomberg found no evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted hardware to the facility. Megaspeed, recently blacklisted by the U.S., denies wrongdoing. Nvidia did not respond to questions.

*Poland has signed its first binding contract with Palantir ($PLTR) to supply its armed forces with the AI-powered Maven Smart System, codenamed Saturn, marking a major step in modernizing the country's military command systems.*

• *Military Capabilities* — Saturn combines data from drones, satellites, radars and intelligence systems to support battlefield management, target identification, logistics and operational recommendations. Final decisions remain with military commanders.
• *NATO Integration* — Maven is used by U.S., NATO and Ukrainian forces. Compatibility with NATO command systems was a key selection criterion for Poland.
• *Data Sovereignty* — Polish intelligence services vetted the software. Poland will retain full control over military data and user access across classified and unclassified networks. Palantir will receive no encryption keys, remote access or access to military data.

*Tesla ($TSLA) may have to wait until 2028 to deploy its next-generation AI5 chip at scale in electric vehicles, as limited TSMC 3nm manufacturing capacity is expected to favor Google and Microsoft data center projects, according to Taiwanese supply-chain sources.*

• *Capacity Constraints* — GUC, Tesla's AI5 chip design partner, has secured substantially more 2027 production capacity from TSMC *($TSM)*, but allocations remain insufficient to meet all major customer demand.
• *Cloud Priority* — GUC reportedly will prioritize Google's *($GOOGL)* Axion 2 and Axion 3 server processors and Microsoft's *($MSFT)* custom chips due to higher margins and greater order visibility.
• *Optimus First* — Elon Musk indicated AI5 will initially prioritize Optimus humanoid robots and Tesla's data centers, while mass-produced vehicles continue using AI4 and AI4.5.
• *Vehicle Rollout* — FSD v15 improves AI4's computing efficiency through algorithmic compression and feature reuse, giving Tesla more time until manufacturing capacity expands enough to support widespread AI5 deployment, potentially in 2028.

*U.S. holiday spending is projected to rise 5.4% YoY, or 2.8% adjusted for inflation, despite consumers reducing budgets and gift lists. Adobe Analytics expects nearly $13B in online Black Friday spending.*

• *Consumer Pressure* — Average planned holiday spending fell to $779 from $796 last year. More than 80% of surveyed shoppers plan to manage costs by purchasing cheaper gifts or shopping for fewer people.
• *Early Spending* — Recent technology outages triggered stockpiling at Walmart *($WMT)*, Costco *($COST)* and Tractor Supply *($TSCO)*. Spending on cleaning products, personal hygiene supplies and baby items rose more than 30% MoM in early November.
• *Shopping Trends* — Thanksgiving weekend shopper turnout is expected to decline for the first time since the pandemic, partly reflecting earlier promotional deals.
• *Income Divide* — Wealthier households are expected to drive spending growth. Only households earning at least $200,000 annually indicated plans to spend more than last year in a Conference Board survey.

*Google ($GOOGL) is reportedly pursuing custom HBM5 memory for its next-generation AI chips, with MediaTek emerging as a leading candidate to design key components for its 10th-generation TPU, potentially shifting greater control over memory design to AI chip developers.*

• *Custom Memory* — Analysts expect the next-generation TPU involving MediaTek to feature 512GB of HBM5. MediaTek is also a leading candidate to design its high-speed data interfaces and HBM base die, which connects stacked memory to the AI processor.
• *Intel Packaging* — Google reportedly plans to adopt Intel's *($INTC)* EMIB-T advanced packaging technology starting with its MediaTek-developed ninth-generation TPU to secure additional packaging capacity and support larger chip packages.
• *Performance Gains* — Customizing the HBM base die for specific AI processors could improve data processing speeds and power efficiency.
• *Memory Competition* — Following Nvidia's *($NVDA)* unveiling of its custom NVHBM architecture in August, Google's initiative raises concerns that Samsung and SK Hynix could lose some control over HBM design to major AI chip developers.
